newsitem.title: WESTERN SAMOA: RUGBY UNION-SAMOA CONFIDENT FOR HOME MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SAMOA CONFIDENT FOR HOME MATCHES.

text.p: Western Samoa are in confident mood for a heavy home programme after thumping Ireland on home turf last year, flanker Sila Vaifale said on Wednesday.

Ireland can look forward with some trepidation to their June 14 rematch with the Samoans, who are unbeaten at Apia Park since 1990, after being dealt a 40-25 lesson in southern hemisphere running rugby in Dublin in November.
The Samoans then play the New Zealand Maoris, Tonga and world sevens champions Fiji in consecutive weeks.
Fiji, who whipped Samoa 60-0 in Suva last year during the annual Pacific Tri series, remain the biggest threat.
"We have a new generation of players coming through now and after our tour to Britain at the end of last year, the team is really coming on," said Vaifale, who has 45 caps.
"If we stay injury free there is every chance to build on that winning form," he said.
He said a win against Ireland in their first visit to Samoa would be crucial to Samoa maintaining international credibility.
"They (Ireland) will be going for the win but we are not going to just stand there and watch it happen."
So far, only centre George Leaupepe, who plays provincial rugby for Counties in New Zealand, is unavailable from the regular test lineup after a torn achillies tendon ruled him out for the season.
Rugby union officials are keen to regain the services of several overseas-based players, including million dollar Newcastle winger Vaaiga Tuigamala, who proved inspiration in the Lansdowne Road win.
Vaifale said Tuigamala, who has switched back to union from league and is one of union's most expensive players, is keen to resume playing for his country as is Bedford flanker Junior Paramore.
